objective: Exploratory experiment. From one parity knot, grow hub-free parity laws by five uniform rules that act only at open ends: R1 sprout at a uniformly random open end; R2 sprout at a knot holding two or more open ends; R3 close the nearest pair of open ends by bond distance, else sprout; R4 as R3 but never make a closing that creates a pinned or tied distinction; R5 sprout at a random open end, then close pairs at bond distance exactly 6 (the flat face size for three-place knots) without pins or ties. Measure exact bond distance (minimum connected cut) from a seed distinction outward, bond-ball growth, pinned links, open ends and cycle rank against size, and classify each rule as ruler, collapse, decoupled cells, small world or unresolved.
status: Closed, supported (exploratory, OPEN-END-GROWTH-20261107-001A-E001): five uniform rules acting only at open ends, exact bond distances. Growing at knots holding two open ends gives the two-way thread, a ruler of dimension one (slope 1.00; balls 4 per unit radius). Random sprouting gives a tree (small world). Greedy closing seals cells (74 pinned seams; no knot for 370 of 374 pairs). Closing that never creates a pin or tie gives a closed strip whose bond distance stays at most 5 (collapse). Flat-face closing gives a small world (largest bond distance 11 at 300 knots). No rule grew a plane. The frozen R2 offset control was mis-specified (seam source; offsets 1 or 2) and is recorded as failed as written; exactness is proved in ticket B.
title: A census of growth rules at open ends
